intro: Lesson 69: Mastery 3: Macbeth: ambition, guilt and key quotations. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

timeline.text: 'Stars, hide your fires': ambition he wants hidden
'Will all great Neptune's ocean wash this blood / Clean from my hand?'
'O, full of scorpions is my mind'

parts.text: Point: as a force that destroys itself
Technique: metaphor of a rider leaping onto a horse
Zoom in: 'o'erleaps' suggests jumping too far and falling
Context: a Jacobean audience saw regicide as against God's order
Link: Macbeth predicts his own fall

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Shakespeare presents ambition as self-destroying: the metaphor of 'vaulting ambition' that 'o'erleaps itself' pictures a rider who jumps too far and falls, foreshadowing Macbeth's ruin.

panels.title: A moral lens
points: Islam teaches that each person is accountable for their own choices
Temptation is real, but the choice remains ours

keywords.def: a strong desire to succeed or gain power
the feeling of having done wrong
a great figure who falls because of a flaw or choice
from the time of King James I (1603 to 1625)

questions.q: Put three quotations in order: 'Out, damned spot!', 'Vaulting ambition', 'Neptune's ocean'
questions.a: Vaulting ambition (1.7), Neptune's ocean (2.2), Out, damned spot! (5.1)

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write a PETZAAL paragraph: How does Shakespeare present guilt?
Extend: write a thesis answering 'villain or victim?'
Stretch: compare Macbeth's guilt with Lady Macbeth's
Which evidence best supports 'Macbeth is a victim'?
options: the witches' prophecies and Lady Macbeth's pressure
questions.a: C) the witches' prophecies and Lady Macbeth's pressure. Outside influences support the victim reading; the other actions are his own choices.
